To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neutrino mass mechanism in the model predicts lepton flavor violating LQ decays and the possibility of LQ cascade decays at the LHC, and that the model is testable at the LHC.

(i) LQs can be produced at the LHC, (ii) LQs explain neutrino oscillation, (iii) LQs decay via the same Yukawas that generate neutrino masses, (iv) the LQ model predicts large LFV rates, and (v) the LQ mechanism can be tested at the LHC.
LQs with TeV masses can be produced at the LHC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of LQ models which are able to explain the observed pattern of neutrino mixing and oscillations.
the phenomenological implications of a new mechanism for neutrino mass generation, which is based on leptoquarks and electroweak gauge bosons.
the interplay between neutrino physics and LHC physics in a model where LQs explain neutrino oscillation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LQs are not the smoking gun of neutrino mass generation.
the LQ model is not only a promising explanation of current neutrino data but also an excellent laboratory for studying lepton flavor violating processes at the LHC.
the LQ mechanism for neutrino mass generation is a viable possibility that can be probed in the near future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while LQs can provide a natural explanation of neutrino masses and mixing, they are not the most economical way to generate neutrino masses.
the LQ explanation of neutrino oscillations is in principle testable, but only at the expense of a rather large LQ mass scale.
, in the leptoquark model for neutrino masses, the LQs at the TeV scale are not only a possible explanation for the origin of the neutrino masses but can also be discovered at the LHC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LQ models are not just interesting from an accelerator phenomenology point of view, they also provide a natural explanation of the observed neutrino masses and mixing angles.
lepton flavor violation and Higgs decays into leptoquark pairs provide the best prospects for probing the LQ origin of neutrino masses at the LHC.
